canonical_statement: The review summarizes current IBD pathogenic mechanisms with emphasis on innate and adaptive immune dysregulation and evaluates established and emerging therapeutic paradigms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review summarizes recent advances in understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms driving IBD, focusing on innate and adaptive immune networks.

canonical_statement: The authors frame integrated, multitarget approaches as the emerging therapeutic frontier for IBD.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review underscores a paradigm shift from monotherapies to integrated, multitarget approaches as the new frontier in IBD management.

canonical_statement: The review characterizes IBD as a chronic immune-mediated disorder arising from convergent genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and microbial perturbations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: atory bowel disease (IBD) | innate and adaptive immunity | mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) | microbiota alterations | precision medicine ABSTRACT Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), which includes ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease, represents a chronic, immune-mediated pathology in which genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and microbial perturbations converge to destabilize intestinal homeostasis. Despite a steady global rise in incidence affecting more than 10 million peop

canonical_statement: The review states that more than 10 million people worldwide are affected by IBD and that 30–40% of patients remain without durable remission on current single-pathway biologic or small-molecule therapies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Despite a steady global rise in incidence affecting more than 10 million people worldwide, current single-pathway biologic and small-molecule therapies still leave 30–40% of patients without durable remission, with progression to stricturing, fistulizing, or transmural complications.

canonical_statement: The review estimates that pediatric-onset IBD is increasing by approximately 1.2% per year.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Pediatric-onset disease is the fastest-growing demographic, expanding by approximately 1.2% per year, with implications for lifetime disease burden and healthcare-system planning.

canonical_statement: The review states that 30–40% of patients with Crohn’s disease require intestinal resection within 10 years of diagnosis and 30–40% of patients receiving biologic therapy lose response within 1–3 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Despite substantial therapeutic progress, real-world outcomes remain suboptimal: 30–40% of patients with CD still require intestinal resection within 10 years of diagnosis, and 30–40% of patients on biologic therapy lose response within 1–3 years [ 6 ].

canonical_statement: IBD pathogenesis is described as a multifactorial interaction among genetic predisposition, environmental factors, immune dysregulation, and altered gut microbiota.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is now clear that the pathogenesis of IBD is multifactorial, involving a complex and poorly understood interplay between genetic predisposition, environmental risk factors (smoking, antibiotic use, and diet), immune dysregulation, and alterations in the gut microbiota.

canonical_statement: The authors organize IBD pathogenesis around an immunome–exposome–genome–microbiome framework.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is now evident that IBD cannot be cured without taking into account the intricate interplay among systemic and mucosal immune systems (immunome) [ 16 ], together with the other components contributing to IBD pathogenesis: exposome (exter- nal and internal environments) [ 17 ], genome (genetic makeup) [ 18 ], and microbiome (gut-dwelling bacteria, fungi, viruses, and archaea) [ 19 ] (Figure 1 ).

canonical_statement: Gut-associated lymphoid tissue is described as balancing protective antigen sampling with tolerance to commensal and dietary antigens, with disruption contributing to barrier breakdown and impaired mucosal repair.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: GALT comprises both organized structures, including Peyer’s patches and isolated lymphoid follicles, and diffuse aggregates of immune cells within the lamina propria [ 22 ] (Figure 2 ).

canonical_statement: Neutrophils are characterized as dual-effect cells in IBD: excessive activation and NET formation can aggravate mucosal injury, whereas neutrophil-derived mediators can also support epithelial repair and resolution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nevertheless, neutrophils and NETs exhibit a dual role in IBD [ 37, 38 ].

canonical_statement: The review describes ILC3-derived IL-22 as context dependent: physiologic IL-22 supports mucosal integrity, while excessive IL-22 may recruit neutrophils and worsen epithelial injury.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: circumstances, ILC3s contribute to mucosal integrity through IL-22 secretion [ 61, 62 ] but dysregulation, especially excessive IL-22 production, may paradoxically exacerbate inflammation by recruiting neutrophils and compromising the epithelial barrier [ 63, 64 ].

canonical_statement: Homeostatic colonic macrophages are described as phagocytic, relatively TLR-hyporesponsive, and constitutive IL-10 producers that support mucosal tolerance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Under homeostatic conditions, colonic macrophages typically express CX3CR1 and Major Histocom- patibility Complex (MHC) II, exhibit robust phagocytic activity, low responsiveness to Toll-like receptor (TLR) stimulation, and constitutively produce IL-10 [ 70 ], thereby contributing to mucosal tolerance.

canonical_statement: Macrophage IL-10 receptor signaling is presented as essential for anti-inflammatory function and mucosal healing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Importantly, signaling through the IL-10 receptor (IL-10R) is essential for anti-inflammatory macrophage functions and mucosal healing [ 78–80 ].

canonical_statement: Aberrantly activated macrophages are implicated in intestinal fibrosis through profibrotic mediators and macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Yet macrophages can also contribute to long-term complications.

canonical_statement: Dendritic-cell dysregulation in IBD is described as loss of protective subsets and increased proinflammatory cytokine production that promotes Th1 responses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In IBD, however, colonic DCs often display immature phenotypes with altered receptor expres- sion [ 94–96 ] and reduced representation of beneficial subsets [ 97 ].

canonical_statement: Inflamed IBD mucosa is described as shifting from protective IgA dominance toward IgG predominance, with anticommensal IgG implicated in UC inflammation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Inflamed intestinal tissues in IBD are characterized by a shift from protective IgA dominance toward IgG predominance [ 106, 107 ].

canonical_statement: Th1 and Th17 effector responses are identified as major adaptive immune contributors to IBD inflammation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Among CD4+ effector cells, T helper 1 (Th1) and T helper 17 (Th17) subsets, that produce IFN- γ and IL- 17A, IL-17F, and IL-22, respectively, have been implicated in both murine and human IBD [ 113, 114 ].

canonical_statement: The review notes that increased Treg numbers in inflamed IBD tissue may coexist with functional impairment or phenotypic plasticity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Unexpectedly, increased numbers of Treg cells have been observed in inflamed IBD tissues [ 115 ], potentially reflecting functional impairment or transient FOXP3 expression.

canonical_statement: Tissue-resident memory T cells are described as enriched in inflamed UC and Crohn’s mucosa and capable of contributing to chronic inflammation and barrier disruption.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells (CD4+ /CD8+ CD69+ CD103+ ) are enriched in inflamed mucosa of UC and CD patients, where they contribute to chronic inflammation and epithelial barrier disruption [ 117, 118 ].

canonical_statement: UC and Crohn’s disease are distinguished by different immune polarization and tissue-injury patterns: UC is predominantly continuous and mucosal, whereas Crohn’s disease is discontinuous and transmural with a stronger Th1/Th17 profile.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: UC is characterized by continuous, mucosa-restricted inflammation of the colon dominated by a Th2-like cytokine profile featuring IL-13, IL-5, and atypical Th17 responses; the inflammatory infiltrate remains largely superficial, sparing the muscularis.

canonical_statement: The review reports that IL-17A/IL-17RA blockade paradoxically worsened Crohn’s disease in randomized trials, consistent with a barrier-protective role for intestinal IL-17A.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Conversely, selective anti-IL-17A (secukinumab) and anti- IL-17RA (brodalumab) antibodies, despite a strong mechanistic rationale, paradoxically worsened CD in randomized trials and have led to new-onset IBD cases in psoriasis cohorts treated with IL-17 inhibitors, a phenomenon attributed to the indispensable barrier-protective role of IL-17A in intestinal epithelium [ 126 ].

canonical_statement: The review reports that the 2024 PROFILE trial favored early top-down infliximab plus immunomodulator therapy over accelerated step-up treatment in newly diagnosed Crohn’s disease regardless of the tested prognostic T-cell biomarker subgroup.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The 2024 PROFILE trial demonstrated that newly diagnosed CD patients benefit substantially from a top- down strategy of early combination immunosuppression with infliximab plus immunomodulator over an accelerated step- up approach, irrespective of the prognostic T-cell biomarker subgroup [ 127 ].

canonical_statement: Genome-wide association studies are summarized as identifying more than 240 IBD risk loci involving microbial sensing, autophagy, epithelial barrier, and immune pathways.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Genome-wide association studies have identified over 240 risk loci affecting microbial sensing (e.g., NOD2 ), autophagy ( ATG16L1 ), epithelial barrier genes ( ECM1 ), and immune path- ways ( IL23R , IL10 ) [ 128, 129, 130, 131, 132 ].

canonical_statement: The review states that known genetic variants explain only 8–13% of Crohn’s disease and 4–7% of ulcerative colitis heritability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, these variants explain only 8–13% of CD and 4–7% of UC heritability [ 133 ].

canonical_statement: Epigenetic alterations, including DNA methylation and miRNA signatures, are described as linked to IBD susceptibility, activity, behavior, and colorectal-cancer risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Epigenomic profiling has revealed that DNA methylation and miRNA signatures are altered in IBD, with distinct pat- terns correlating with disease susceptibility, activity, behavior, and colorectal cancer (CRC) risk [ 135, 136, 137, 138, 139, 140, 141 ].

canonical_statement: Oncostatin M overexpression is presented as a tissue feature associated with anti-TNF treatment failure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Other studies have pinpointed at genes overexpressed in IBD tissue, such as oncostatin M, predictive of anti-TNF therapy failure [ 149 ].

canonical_statement: The GIMATS cellular module is described as enriched in a subgroup of ileal Crohn’s disease and associated with lack of durable remission after anti-TNF therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For instance, the GIMATS cellular module, encompassing IgG-producing plasma cells, inflammatory mononuclear phagocytes, activated T cells, and stromal cells, was found to be enriched in a subgroup of patients with ileal CD and associated with a lack of durable remission following anti-TNF therapy [ 106 ].

canonical_statement: CARD15/NOD2 variants are described as associated with Crohn’s disease but not ulcerative colitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For example, CARD15/NOD2 mutations, functionally linked to a deficient antimicrobial defense, are significantly associated with risk of CD and not with UC [ 153 ].

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that single-locus susceptibility signals have rarely translated into individual predictive biomarkers and argue for composite multiomic stratification.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The therapeu- tic translation of such genetic signals, however, has been uneven: while anti-IL-12/23 strategies validated the IL-12/23 axis in CD, single-locus susceptibility variants have so far rarely translated into individual-patient predictive biomarkers, underscoring the need for composite, multiomic stratification approaches.

canonical_statement: IBD-associated dysbiosis is described as reduced microbial diversity, relative enrichment of potentially pathogenic taxa, and depletion of beneficial short-chain-fatty-acid producers such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Roseburia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Specific bacterial groups like Enter- obacteriaceae , Fusobacterium spp ., and Ruminococcus gnavus are frequently overrepresented in active IBD, while beneficial species such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Roseburia spp ., crucial producers of SCFAs with anti-inflammatory properties, are often diminished [ 159, 160, 161 ].

canonical_statement: The review links reduced microbial short-chain fatty acid production and altered bile-acid and tryptophan metabolism to impaired intestinal homeostasis and inflammatory signaling in IBD.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Specific bacterial groups like Enter- obacteriaceae , Fusobacterium spp ., and Ruminococcus gnavus are frequently overrepresented in active IBD, while beneficial species such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Roseburia spp ., crucial producers of SCFAs with anti-inflammatory properties, are often diminished [ 159, 160, 161 ].

canonical_statement: The review describes disease-associated differences across the bacteriome, mycobiome, and virome between ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Some studies focused on highlighting differences in bacteriome, mycobiome, and virome between UC and CD.

canonical_statement: Microbiome-directed interventions discussed include diet, bacteriophages, defined bacterial consortia, and engineered probiotic organisms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Beyond these, advanced biotechnological approaches are under development, including bacteriophages [ 178 ] designed to pre- cisely target specific pathogenic bacteria and rationally defined bacterial consortia (US National Library of Medicine.

canonical_statement: The review explicitly states that no causal link has yet been established between microbiome alterations and IBD.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although no causal link has been established between micro- biome alterations and IBD, the potential for microbiota-based treatments, such as FMT, has been proposed (see Section 3.2).

canonical_statement: The review reports that after 54 weeks of infliximab therapy, clinical remission was observed in about 25% of Crohn’s disease patients and 35% of ulcerative colitis patients in the cited studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, clinical remission was observed in only 25% of patients with CD [ 183 ] and in 35% of patients with UC after 54 weeks of infliximab treat- ment [ 184 ].

canonical_statement: Ustekinumab is described as an IL-12/23 p40 inhibitor with efficacy in both Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, including clinical and histo-endoscopic outcomes in cited registration programs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For example, antibodies, such as ustekinumab, which targets the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, have been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) based on demonstrated effectiveness in treating CD and UC [ 190, 191, 192 ].

canonical_statement: The review reports that risankizumab maintenance in Crohn’s disease produced Week-52 clinical remission rates of 52% versus 41% and endoscopic response rates of 47% versus 22% compared with placebo in the cited FORTIFY program.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Additionally, the FORTIFY trials [ 196 ] confirmed the sustained efficacy of risankizumab during the maintenance phase at Week 52, with clinical remission rates of 52 versus 41% and endoscopic response rates of 47 versus 22% when compared with placebo.

canonical_statement: The review reports that mirikizumab in VIVID-1 achieved clinical remission of 45.4% versus 19.6% and endoscopic response of 38% versus 9% compared with placebo in moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In this study, patients treated with mirikizumab achieved significantly higher rates of clinical remission (45.4 vs.

canonical_statement: The review states that IL-17A or IL-17RA antibodies have not shown efficacy in Crohn’s disease and have caused disease worsening.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In contrast to anti IL- 12/IL-23 antibodies, those against IL-17A or the IL-17 receptor subunit IL-17RA have not demonstrated effectiveness in CD [ 126 ] and even caused disease worsening, which prevented their approval for treating patients with IBD.

canonical_statement: Vedolizumab is described as a gut-selective α4β7-integrin antibody effective for induction of clinical remission in Crohn’s disease, with a different safety profile from natalizumab.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In contrast, vedolizumab, a monoclonal antibody against α4 β7 integrin, has received approval for treating CD based on its ability to induce clinical remission in both patients exposed or not exposed to anti-TNF- α therapy, as evidenced by the GEMINI-2 study [ 212 ].

canonical_statement: Tofacitinib is described as effective and approved for ulcerative colitis, whereas cited randomized trials did not show superiority over placebo in Crohn’s disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Tofacitinib is a pan-JAK inhibitor, which, acting either on JAK1 and JAK3 enzymes, blocks signals from IL-12, IL-23, and other cytokines by inhibiting downstream signaling pathways.

canonical_statement: The SELECTION trial is summarized as showing filgotinib induction remission rates of 26.1% versus 15.3% in biologic-naive patients and 11.5% versus 4.2% in previously exposed patients, with maintenance remission of 37.2% versus 11.2%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The SELECTION study [ 221 ] demonstrated that filgotinib was more effective than placebo in inducing remission at Week 10 among patients without prior exposure (26.1 vs.

canonical_statement: Upadacitinib is identified as the only JAK inhibitor approved for Crohn’s disease at the time of the review, supported by U-EXCEL, U-EXCEED, and U-ENDURE.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: At present, upadacitinib is the only JAK inhibitor approved for the treatment of CD, supported by the positive results from two Phase III induction trials (U-EXCEL and U-EXCEED) as well as and the Phase III maintenance trial (U-ENDURE) [ 222 ].

canonical_statement: The ozanimod open-label extension is summarized as maintaining clinical response in 91.4%, clinical remission in 69.1%, and corticosteroid-free status in 67.9% at Week 94 of the extension.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Furthermore, the OLE study [ 226 ] revealed sustained benefits, with 91.4% of patients maintaining clinical response, 69.1% maintaining clinical remission, and 67.9% remaining corticosteroid-free at Week 94 of the OLE (146 weeks total treatment).

canonical_statement: The ELEVATE program is summarized as showing etrasimod clinical remission of 27% versus 7% at Week 12 and 32% versus 7% at Week 52 in ulcerative colitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ELEVATE study [ 227 ] demonstrated etrasimod effectiveness in ameliorating clinical remission at induction (Week 12: 27 vs.

canonical_statement: The review describes STRIDE-II treat-to-target goals as extending from symptom and biomarker control toward mucosal, histologic, endoscopic, and transmural healing outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In this regard, STRIDE-II guidelines [ 228 ] promote treat-to-target strategy with short-term (symptom relief, biomarker normalization) and long-term goals (mucosal healing, remission, no disability).

canonical_statement: The authors identify heterogeneous endpoint definitions, trial designs, populations, prior treatment exposure, data acquisition, and analyses as major barriers to cross-trial comparison of IBD therapies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Furthermore, the marked heterogeneity in IBD trials given not only to different endpoint definitions, but also to different clinical trial design, patient populations, previous treatment exposure, data acquisition, and analytical approaches, makes it difficult to compare clinical trial results of different therapeutic agents in IBD.

canonical_statement: The review calls for randomized head-to-head trials supplemented by network meta-analysis and real-world comparative studies to better position IBD therapies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Despite the availability of multiple mechanisms of action, comparative effectiveness data remain sparse, with only a few head-to-head trials offering direct guidance on sequencing therapies.

canonical_statement: Obefazimod is described as an emerging ulcerative-colitis therapy that increases miR-124 expression and downregulates proinflammatory pathways.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Later, obefazimod was found to raise miR-124 levels, which in turn decreased proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-17 and IL-6, both in an IBD mouse model and in patients with UC [ 243 ].

canonical_statement: The review reports sustained obefazimod results at Week 96, including 52.5% clinical remission and 59.0% endoscopic improvement in the cited Phase IIb extension.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: At Week 96, 52.5% of patients achieved clinical remission, closely mirroring the 54.8% remission rate observed at Week 48.

canonical_statement: The review states that fecal microbiota transplantation induced remission in three of four randomized controlled trials in ulcerative colitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 3.2.2 Fecal Microbiota Transplantation FMT has demonstrated the capacity to induce remission in three [ 246–248 ] of four randomized controlled trials in UC [ 249 ] (Figure 3 ).

canonical_statement: FMT is described as limited by lack of standardized protocols, modest or transient benefit, and safety concerns including transmission of multidrug-resistant organisms and pathogens.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, its therapeutic application remains constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, the modest and often transient nature of clinical benefit, and ongoing safety concerns.

canonical_statement: The authors state that current FMT evidence supports at most modest benefit in carefully selected ulcerative-colitis patients and does not support standard-care adoption.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although current evidence suggests FMT can achieve modest benefit in carefully selected UC patients [ 246, 248 ], its overall efficacy is limited and does not support adoption as standard care.

canonical_statement: The review states that approximately 11% of ulcerative-colitis patients and up to 70% of Crohn’s-disease patients ultimately require surgery because of refractory disease or complications.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Approximately 11% of patients with UC and up to 70% of patients with CD ultimately require surgery owing to refractory disease or complications [ 264 ].

canonical_statement: Preclinical MSC studies are summarized as generally improving survival, disease activity, colon length, histopathology, inflammatory-cell infiltration, and cytokine profiles in experimental IBD models.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most preclinical studies consistently report that MSC treatment significantly leads to significant improvements in several IBD parameters, such as increased survival rates, reduced DAI, longer colon length, and better histopathological outcomes [ 280, 295, 296 ] (see Table 3 ).

canonical_statement: Cell-free MSC approaches using conditioned medium, extracellular vesicles, or exosomes are described as producing beneficial outcomes in preclinical IBD models.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Positive outcomes have been achieved using cell-free strategies, such as conditioned medium (CM)/secretome from MSC cultures (CM- MSC) [ 288, 297, 298, 299, 300, 301 ] and EVs or exosomes extracted from CM-MSC [ 284, 302, 303, 304, 305, 306 ].

canonical_statement: The review notes that MSC preclinical findings are not uniformly positive and that tissue source, route, dose, and timing remain important unresolved variables.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: While the majority of studies report positive results, a limited number show negative or conflicting outcomes.

canonical_statement: Typical single MSC doses in preclinical mouse studies are summarized as 1–10 × 10^6 cells, with no established optimal dose across cell, conditioned-medium, or extracellular-vesicle products.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dose-dependent benefits have been reported [ 281, 285 ], with typical single doses ranging from 1 to 10 × 106 MSCs per mouse [ 313 ].

canonical_statement: The review identifies T-cell suppression, Treg expansion, macrophage M2 polarization, and paracrine mediators as central mechanisms of MSC/MSC-EV immunomodulation in experimental IBD.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Preclinical data identify immunomodulation of T-cell and macrophage responses as the therapeutically dominant mecha- nism by which MSCs ameliorate IBD.

canonical_statement: In ADMIRE-CD, darvadstrocel is reported to have achieved Week-24 combined remission of 51.5% versus 35.6% with placebo in 212 patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Darvadstrocel (Cx601, Alofisel), an expanded allogeneic adipose- derived MSC product for complex Crohn’s perianal fistulas, showed benefit in the Phase III ADMIRE-CD trial ( n = 212): com- bined remission at Week 24 was 51.5 versus 35.6% with placebo ( p = 0.021), with sustained benefit to 52 and 104 weeks [ 344– 346 ].

canonical_statement: The larger ADMIRE-CD II trial is reported as failing its primary endpoint, with combined remission of 48.8% versus 46.3% and p=0.571 in 568 patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, the larger ADMIRE-CD II ( n = 568) failed to meet its primary endpoint (combined remission 48.8 vs.

canonical_statement: The review concludes that local MSC injections have stronger long-term evidence for perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease than systemic MSC infusions for luminal IBD, where results remain mixed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Strong evidence supports the long-term efficacy of local MSC injections for perianal fistuliz- ing CD, while data on systemic MSC infusions for luminal IBD show mixed results.

canonical_statement: The review distinguishes pharmacokinetic anti-TNF failure from pharmacodynamic failure and describes secondary loss of response as often related to low drug concentrations, antidrug antibodies, or shifts in inflammatory pathways.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary nonresponse to advanced therapies, such as anti-TNF therapies, is most commonly explained by two mechanisms: pharmacokinetic problems (fast drug clearance leading to low blood levels) or pharmacodynamic failure (inflam- mation mediated by alternative pathways to the mechanism targeted by the allocated therapy) [ 348, 349 ].

canonical_statement: Infliximab plus azathioprine is described as superior to monotherapy for corticosteroid-free clinical remission in both Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis in cited Phase III evidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Notably, Phase III trials have demonstrated that infliximab in combination with azathioprine is superior to monotherapy for inducing corticosteroid-free clinical remission in both CD and UC, with additional benefits including reduced antidrug antibody formation and fewer infusion reactions [ 356 ].

canonical_statement: Dual-biologic and small-molecule–biologic combinations are described as promising but limited by small observational cohorts, inadequate long-term safety data, and cost.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Preliminary evidence from small observational studies suggests that combinations such as tofacitinib with vedolizumab or ustekinumab may be effective in achieving clin- ical and endoscopic remission in selected individuals [ 359, 360 ].

canonical_statement: The review highlights FMT risks including transfer of harmful organisms, antibiotic-resistance genes, and virulence factors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is especially alarming amid rising antibiotic resistance, as FMT could inadvertently transmit resis- tance genes and virulence factors, resulting in serious unintended consequences.

canonical_statement: The HLA-DQA1*05 allele is described as present in approximately 40% of Europeans and associated with roughly doubled immunogenicity-driven loss of response to infliximab and adalimumab.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Second, the HLA-DQA1*05 allele—present in approximately 40% of Europeans—doubles the rate of immunogenicity-driven loss of response to infliximab and adalimumab [ 350 ]; these patients are predicted to derive added benefit from concomi- tant immunomodulator therapy or from early non-TNF biologic strategies.

canonical_statement: The PROFILE study is cited as showing that a prognostic T-cell signature did not identify patients who differentially benefited from early combined immunosuppression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The biomarker-stratified PROFILE study [ 127 ] found that the prognostic T-cell signature did not differen- tiate patients who benefited from early combined immuno- suppression, indicating that current single-biomarker assays are insufficient and that composite biomarker signatures inte- grating genetic, transcriptomic, microbial, and serological data are required.

canonical_statement: The authors propose that future IBD precision trials use composite genetic, transcriptomic, microbial, and serologic biomarkers rather than single-marker stratification.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The biomarker-stratified PROFILE study [ 127 ] found that the prognostic T-cell signature did not differen- tiate patients who benefited from early combined immuno- suppression, indicating that current single-biomarker assays are insufficient and that composite biomarker signatures inte- grating genetic, transcriptomic, microbial, and serological data are required.

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that single-target anti-inflammatory therapies frequently fail to produce durable remission and that future strategies should address multiple pathogenic mechanisms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 4.2 Limitations of Current Therapeutic Strategies Existing treatments predominantly target single inflammatory mediators or immune pathways.

canonical_statement: The review identifies miRNA-124 regulation, microbiota restoration, and regenerative cell-based therapies as prominent multitarget or nontraditional therapeutic opportunities.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Promising interventions include the regulation of gene expression via miRNA-124, the restoration of microbial equilibrium through FMT, and regenerative cell- based therapies.

canonical_statement: Clinical translation of MSC-based therapies is described as constrained by variability in cell sources, dosing, administration, manufacturing, potency assessment, regulatory definitions, donor factors, and cryopreservation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, substantial barriers to translation persist.

canonical_statement: The review’s final outlook favors precision-guided immune re-education and mucosal restoration over isolated single-pathway inhibition.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 4.5 Outlook The future of IBD management lies in moving beyond inflammation control toward immune re-education and mucosal restoration, guided by precision medicine principles.
